text: Richard George Whittle, born on 31 December 1979 in Oldham, England, to Harry and Maggie (Goodwin) Whittle, is a British actor and the oldest of three children. His mother is English and his father is Jamaican; his father served in the Royal Air Force, causing the family to move to different countries every few years. Whittle was primarily raised in Northern Ireland and recalled being bullied as a child for being the only black child in school, at one point telling his mother he wanted to be white to fit in. He studied law at Southampton Solent University, where he was football team captain, and began modelling to pay for textbooks, eventually leaving university just before graduation. He took up modelling in college and became the face of Reebok in 2000. Whittle made his acting debut in 2002 on the Sky 1 series Dream Team, which he described as a "dream job," after being sent for an audition by his co-star Terence Maynard. He left the show in 2006 and joined Channel 4's soap opera Hollyoaks in May 2006 as Calvin Valentine. In December 2009, it was announced he would leave Hollyoaks, with the character killed off in 2010; he cited plans to pursue American television and film and intended to stay for only four years. In summer 2009, he competed in Series 7 of the BBC reality show Strictly Come Dancing, pairing with professional dancer Natalie Lowe, and finished second to Chris Hollins. He permanently relocated to Los Angeles in summer 2011. Upon arriving in the US, he met with someone to create an audition reel, leading to a signing with manager Ken Jacobsen, who has also represented James Franco, Michelle Williams, and Hilary Swank. He was cast in the film Austinland opposite Keri Russell, Jane Seymour, and Jennifer Coolidge, joking that his audition tape cut off his head and that the film was shot in the UK despite his move to Los Angeles. His immigration status caused him to withdraw from several projects, including an episode of the NBC sitcom Up All Night, after management informed him the network would not accept his visa, prompting him to apply for a green card. In March 2012, he was cast in a recurring role as Charles on VH1's Single Ladies, initially for two episodes but later expanded to six after making a strong impression on producer Stacy A. Littlejohn, who wrote him into the rest of the season. The series was filmed in Atlanta from January to June 2012. In 2013, he appeared in an episode of the CBS drama NCIS titled "Detour." In 2014, he joined The CW's post-apocalyptic drama The 100 as Lincoln, and on 25 July 2014 at San Diego Comic-Con, it was announced he was promoted to series regular for season 2. Around the same time, he booked a recurring role as Daniel on ABC's Mistresses, the love interest of April (Rochelle Aytes), appearing in 10 episodes. In January 2016, it was reported he was in talks for a lead role on another series; during an April 2016 interview with AfterBuzz TV, he announced his departure from The 100, accusing creator Jason Rothenberg of bullying him by marginalizing his character, and stated that after Warner Bros. Television President Peter Roth and The CW President Mark Pedowitz learned of the situation, he was allowed to audition for other projects. In January 2016, he was cast as Shadow Moon, the lead in Starz's television adaptation of Neil Gaiman's 2001 novel American Gods, opposite Ian McShane. Though he had no prior knowledge of the novel, he was a fan-favorite choice for the role, and out of 2,000 audition tapes submitted, he was selected from approximately 600 actors who met with producers after submitting 16 audition tapes over a five-month period. In September 2017, he was cast opposite Sanaa Lathan in the Netflix original film Nappily Ever After, based on a novel by Trisha R. Thomas. On 16 April 2018, he signed with talent agency William Morris Endeavor. Whittle dated his Hollyoaks co-star Carley Stenson from 2007 to 2009 and remained close friends with her; he dated Kirstina Colonna from 2016 to 2018.
